messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: scability question with rstan
parts:
Hi all,

I ran the following test script for a sense of potential impact of creating large matrices as transformed parameters (for the suppose of fitting  univariate GPs with N up to 2000) in rstan:

data {
  int N;
}
parameters {
  real x;
}
transformed parameters {
  matrix[N, N] Sigma;
  Sigma <- rep_matrix(0, N, N);
}
model {
  x ~ normal(0, 1);
}

I run this in rstan with (system.time(sampling(tt, cores=1, chains=1, data=list(N=X)))

This is the results I get

N        STAN elapsed time    R(User)    R(system)  R(elapsed)
===============================================
100     1.1373                      2.080        0.000        2.083
150     3.01804                    7.576         0.000       7.589
200     5.07317                    22.712       0.212       22.964
250     7.64746                    47.876       0.056       48.010
300     12.2785                    119.988     0.064        120.241
350     17.3833                    287.552     0.120        288.195


It seems that rstan is adding some kind of exponential overhead as N increases.

Is this normal? Does this have something to do with my system config?

many thanks,

Andy

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] scability question with rstan
parts:
It should be N^2, which is what the Stan time looks like.
No idea what's up with RStan here.

With GPs, it'll be N^3 because you need to solve the matrix,
so 2K isn't likely to be very fast!

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] scability question with rstan
parts:
rstan has trouble in getting large amounts of data to and from stan itself. We investigated this a while ago and the reason seems to be some Rcpp weirdness and it was unclear if rstan back then did misuse Rcpp or if Rcpp had an issue. From what I recall rstan (or Rcpp) still has this problem. So passing large stuff around can sometimes be done faster by calling cmdstan, which serializes things as csv and then you read back with read_stan_csv.

Sebastian
